title: Grateful Dead Live at Fox Theatre on 1972-10-18
source: Unknown SBD source (probably shnid 7295) CD > wav > cool edit 2000 > flac

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture with pleasant Bob guitar distortion; standout China Cat > Rider, Playin' in the Band sandwich and a psychedelic Dark Star jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean 1972 soundboard source that offers excellent instrument separation and a unique tonal character, highlighted by a pleasantly distorted Bobby rhythm‑guitar channel. Musically the show shines with a tight China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, an expansive Playin' in the Band sandwich and a long, spacey Dark Star, though one reviewer found the Dark Star a bit dull. Overall energy is high and the mix showcases each member well.

ai_rating.rationale: Four detailed reviews uniformly rate the set 4‑5 stars, praising both performance (especially key jams) and recording clarity; minor criticisms do not outweigh the overall enthusiasm.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundstage with excellent instrument separation; slight distortion in Bob's guitar channel noted as a pleasant character, no major drop‑outs or muddiness.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Dark Star (described as boring by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens tight with a bluesy RxR vibe and early tuning quirks; second set builds into the classic Playin' in the Band sandwich, featuring extended jams, a drum solo, and an unusual Drum > Dark Star transition before concluding with high‑energy encores.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as 'distinctly fingering a meltdown' during the jam, indicating intense lead work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for dominant bass solo and feedback moments; multiple mentions of Phil's strong presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm guitar shows a pleasant distortion that adds character; vocals are also noted as prominent.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted as 'nice in the mix' with good soundstage presence, contributing to the unique 1972 keyboard tone.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill is called 'hard‑drivin'' and even gets a drum solo; unusual Drum > Dark Star transition noted.
